chunks: Abu Ali Al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Safwan, from Abd Allah ibn Muskan, from Ali ibn Abd al-Aziz, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) performed the ritual bath for Ihram, then entered the Masjid al-Shajara and prayed, then went out to the boys and said: 'Bring what you have of the flesh of the game so that we may eat it.'

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لُحُومِ الصَّيْدِ: The flesh/meat of hunted game animals
key_terms.مَسْجَدَ الشَّجَرَةِ: A specific mosque in Mecca associated with the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on eating hunted meat while in the state of Ihram according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi highlights the practical application of Ihram rulings by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him), who consumed hunted game after performing the ritual bath and praying in Masjid al-Shajara. It serves as a foundational evidence for the permissibility of eating hunted meat during Ihram, provided the Talbiyya has not yet been recited, a nuance emphasized by the chapter's title. This incident underscores the Imam's role in clarifying the temporal boundaries of Ihram restrictions within the Shia jurisprudential tradition.
